original_record.subject: mathematics
original_record.question: Find a factor which is common to all three binomial expressions 4a2 – 9b2, a3 + 27b3, (4a + 6b)2
original_record.ai_explanation: Factoring: 4a² - 9b² = (2a + 3b)(2a - 3b), a³ + 27b³ = (a + 3b)(a² - 3ab + 9b²), and (4a + 6b)² = 4(2a + 3b)², so 2a + 3b is the common factor.

candidate.subject: mathematics
candidate.question: Find a factor which is common to all three binomial expressions 4a² − 9b², a³ + 27b³ and (4a + 6b)².
candidate.ai_explanation: First, 4a² − 9b² = (2a − 3b)(2a + 3b), while (4a + 6b)² = 4(2a + 3b)². Their only possible shared nonconstant linear factor is 2a + 3b. But a³ + 27b³ = (a + 3b)(a² − 3ab + 9b²), which is not divisible by 2a + 3b. Therefore none of the listed factors divides all three expressions: option E.
